record.why: A refusal that cannot say why is not a refusal. Written 2026-09-03 (lane T fix pass) out of what this record already holds, and out of nothing else. IT IS NOT THAT NO SUPPLIER WAS FOUND: two offers are here, both `confidence: verified`, both retrieved 2026-09-02 — DigiKey 1662-S-8252AAX-M6T1UCT-ND at USD 2.2200 (1+) falling to 1.10096 at 9 000, and LCSC C468219 S-8252AAC-M6T1U at USD 1.8559 (1+) falling to 1.1234 at 1 000. Three measured things stop this being a PASS. (1) THE TWO OFFERS ARE NOT THE SAME PART: -AAX and -AAC are different detection-voltage option codes of one series (LCSC also lists AAG C468221, AAO C468216, ABB C5904467, AAA-I6T1U C7070591), and this record's own matched_on says they are NOT interchangeable — so what is here is two prices for two parts, not two quotes for one. (2) WHICH OPTION CODE IS FITTED IS UNKNOWN, because the IC is inside the NP-F550 pack (spec/sourcing.json line R3: 'inside the NP-F550 pack, not separately purchased') and no pack has been opened. Until the suffix is known there is nothing to ask a second distributor FOR, which is why the second-source column is empty rather than searched-and-failed. (3) BOTH OFFERS ARE OUT OF STOCK TODAY: DigiKey '0 in stock; 3,000 estimated 23-Dec-2026', LCSC 'Out of Stock' — a lead time no build plan can quote against. WHAT SETTLES IT: open one NP-F550 pack, read the top marking on the SOT-23-6 protection IC (the ABLIC series marks the option code), then re-quote that exact orderable at two distributors with stock and a lead time. The price band is already bounded either way — every option code in the series sits between USD 1.10 and 2.22 at these breaks — so this refusal is about identity and availability, not about cost.
